verdicts.quote: the nurse reviews and confirms before anything reaches Epic

Once they’ve confirmed a note, the nurse needs to be able to see a clear success message, know the note is now in Epic, and move on to the next patient without having to log into another system or check anything manually.
If Epic fails to save the note, the nurse needs to see a clear error message that says what went wrong—like “Connection to Epic failed”—and be given a simple option to retry or flag it for IT.
unconfirmed notes stay saved as drafts
Yes, when a nurse returns, they should see the draft exactly as they left it—same patient, same text, same place in the note—so they don’t lose their work. Drafts should be kept for 72 hours
the confirmation screen should show the note text, the patient’s name, and their unique ID—like their medical record number
the nurse returns to the note from review
the review-screen edit requirement is removed and editing stays on the note screen
After confirming a note and seeing the success message, the system should take them straight to the next patient’s blank note—assuming they’re working through a list in order.
The nurse should see a message saying “Failed to send to Epic. Connection lost. Retry in a few minutes.” The note should stay saved as a draft with the original timestamp and nurse info
The success screen will show the patient's name, medical record number, the note timestamp, the nurse's name, and a confirmation that the note appears in Epic.

Failure message 'Failed to send to Epic. Connection lost. Retry in a few minutes.' is shown - Note stays saved as draft with original timestamp and nurse info - Nurse can retry sending note from draft
They should see a confirmation message that says, “Help request sent successfully. IT will contact you within 15 minutes.” The request should appear in a dedicated IT queue
The review screen should clearly show the note text, patient name, medical record number, and timestamp, with a “Confirm” button and a “Go Back” button.
